one_line_contribution: The claim that an injected memory item's marginal value is a property of the (item, instruction) pair rather than of the item — operationalized by decomposing both the task instruction and each retrieved item into atomic guidance units and labeling each item unit against the instruction as REDUNDANT/NOVEL/CONFLICTING with an off-the-shelf NLI model — together with a per-instance token-matched surgical ablation (drop-redundant vs drop-random vs drop-novel vs decoy-instruction placebo) and a retrieval rule scoring candidates by instruction-conditional novel-unit yield per token.
closest_prior_work: The authors name Sufficient Context (ICLR 2025) and AtomMem as the threats, and they are right that neither uses the instruction as the reference set. The threat they never mention is the query/instruction-conditioned context- and prompt-compression line — LongLLMLingua / LLMLingua-2, RECOMP, Provence and the 2026 context-curation/context-engineering successors. Those systems already prune retrieved context conditioned on the full prompt (which contains the instruction), and their headline result is exactly this proposal's headline deliverable: roughly half the injected tokens at preserved accuracy, beating token-matched random or naive truncation. That literature does not decompose the *instruction* into guidance units, does not produce a three-way taxonomy, and does not run a decoy-instruction placebo, so it does not fully collide — but it makes the practical contribution (S2 and Part 3) look like a re-derivation with heavier machinery, and it is absent from Related Work entirely. Secondary threats the proposal also does not engage: ExpeL's own insight-vs-demonstration split (the instruction/memory division of labour is the framing ExpeL already operates under), and the context-memory knowledge-conflict literature (e.g. Adaptive Chameleon or Stubborn Sloth and successors), which is the established home of the CONFLICTING channel and has already characterized when contextual guidance that contradicts what the model was told is followed or ignored.
strongest_objection: Prediction 1 — the relationality claim the title rests on — is confounded, and it is the one claim with no placebo. I_short and I_long differ in two things at once: content overlap with the memory bank, and the fact that I_long is a GEPA-optimized instruction that independently raises accuracy and lengthens the prompt. Any two independently helpful interventions are generically sub-additive, so S1−S0 shrinking by ≥5 points from I_short to I_long is predicted by ceiling/base-rate mechanics with no reference to unit-level redundancy: under I_long, S0 is higher, so fewer instances remain fixable and more remain breakable, and the paired fix/break table is measured against a different base rate. The proposal built a decoy instruction (S7) precisely to remove the identity of the conditioning text in Part 2, then failed to build the analogous control for Part 1 — there is no length-, register- and optimizer-matched instruction whose content does *not* overlap the bank. As written, the label-distribution shift (≤15% → ≥40% REDUNDANT) and the gain collapse can both occur while the causal story is false. A second, independent problem: the precheck gate requires only that the bank move ≥6% of dev instances 'in either direction', which admits exactly the regime this research track already measured — a bank that fixes zero items and breaks six or seven. In that regime Part 1's fix regression on novel-unit count and prediction 3's clause that S4 'loses ≥5 points of fixes relative to S2' have almost no events to model, and half the paper is unpowered while the precheck reports green. Third, and smaller: S3 (token-matched random deletion) is not an independent control but a diluted S4 — a random subset deletes novel units in proportion, so S2 > S3 follows from S4 hurting, and the only genuinely non-tautological arm is S7, whose construction is under-specified. Under a decoy instruction almost every item unit should label NOVEL, so the decoy-REDUNDANT set will typically be far smaller than the real one, and the proposal never says how S7 is padded to per-instance token match; if it is padded at random, S7 degenerates into S3 and prediction 4 ('S7 recovers less than half of the S2−S3 gap') becomes a statement about the padding rule rather than about instruction identity.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Add an I_long_control arm: an instruction matched to I_long in length, register and optimizer provenance (e.g. GEPA run on a disjoint training split or against a different objective) whose guidance content is largely disjoint from the frozen bank, and pre-register that the redundancy shift and the gain collapse appear for I_long but not I_long_control. Without this the relationality claim cannot be separated from sub-additivity, and it is cheap — one extra optimizer run plus S0/S1 at 500×2. (2) Report fixes and breaks as separate outcomes with base-rate-adjusted contrasts across instruction conditions rather than leaning on net paired deltas whose base rates differ by construction. (3) Tighten the precheck to gate on fix *events* specifically (e.g. ≥25 fixes under at least one instruction), not total movement, since the novel-unit→fix channel is untestable in a fix-free bank and this track has already observed one. (4) Specify S7's token-matching rule exactly and pre-register it — how the decoy-redundant set is extended when it is smaller than the real one — or replace S7 with a shuffled-instruction-assignment placebo (label item units against a *different real instance's* optimized instruction) where the label set is naturally comparable in size. (5) Add an instruction-conditioned compression baseline (below). (6) Budget full-scale LLM labeling as the fallback instrument (~400 items × ~5 units × 2 instructions is well under the stated $100 headroom) so that an NLI–human kappa below 0.6 downgrades the instrument rather than terminating the study; as written, only 400 validation pairs have LLM labels, and DeBERTa-MNLI is out of distribution on imperative-vs-imperative pairs where 'redundant' means near-paraphrase, not entailment. (7) Reconcile the internal inconsistency: the Abstract/Short Hypothesis promise '~half the injected tokens' from dropping redundant units, but prediction 1 sets redundancy at ≤15% of units under I_short and ≥40% under I_long, and unit share is not token share once per-item boilerplate survives deletion. Report realized token savings per instruction condition and scope the equivalence claim to I_long.
missing_baseline: An instruction-conditioned context/prompt-compression baseline at matched injected-token budget — LLMLingua-2, RECOMP, or even a small extractive sentence-selector scoring each item sentence against the instruction — run both as a Part 3 selection/compression rule and as a Part 1 competing regressor. This is the 'LLM-compressor baseline' the proposal explicitly cut, and the stated reason for cutting it is wrong: the justification says MMR tests item-level curation more cleanly, but a compressor conditioned on the instruction is not item-level curation at all — it is the instruction-as-reference-set hypothesis implemented without atomic decomposition, i.e. the single strongest competitor to both the instrument claim and the method claim, and the thing a practitioner would actually deploy. The embedding/lexical overlap proxy is a weaker stand-in and does not cover it. Secondary omissions: (a) the length/optimizer-matched control instruction described above, which is a missing arm rather than a missing method; (b) an instruction-augmentation arm that appends the bank's NOVEL units to the instruction instead of injecting them as retrieved items, which is the direct test of the proposal's own Risk #4 (that guidance must be restated in concrete episodic form to be followed) and is the natural 'why retrieve at all' baseline for a paper whose thesis is that only the novel units carry value.
preprint_collision: The check is more diligent than most: seven named items, a per-item collide/does-not-collide verdict, an explicit retraction of a citation cluster (SkillZip/SkillRAE/SkillOps) the current search failed to reconfirm, and a stated caveat about unindexed OpenReview 2026 submissions with a self-assessed nontrivial collision risk. That is genuine work and I credit it. But it searched the wrong neighbourhood for the contribution it is defending. Every one of the seven items sits in the agent-memory-harm niche; nothing in the search covers prompt or context compression, instruction-aware context pruning, or the 2026 context-engineering/context-curation line, which is precisely where a preprint claiming 'condition pruning on what the prompt already says, cut half the injected tokens at matched accuracy' would appear — and that is the proposal's operational deliverable, not a side result. Nothing covers the context-memory knowledge-conflict literature either, which already studies the CONFLICTING channel under a different name. So the concluding paragraph ('no located work decomposes both the agent instruction and each retrieved memory item into guidance units') is true but weak evidence, because the searches run could not have located such work. I cannot name a specific recent preprint that makes the exact (item unit, instruction unit) marginal-value claim, so I do not treat this as scooped; I do treat the check as establishing novelty for the framing while leaving novelty for the instrument and the method unestablished. The authors' own estimate — that instruction-aware dedup plausibly already exists as an appendix ablation in a contemporaneous context-compilation preprint — strikes me as accurate and, given the missing compression baseline, more damaging than they allow.
